Makow mazowiecki Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Maków Mazowiecki, Poland

Not demolished. Maków Mazowiecki's older Jewish cemetery (see the Maków Mazowiecki New Jewish Cemetery record for the town's fuller community history) suffered significant WWII and postwar damage, with Germans using matzevot for road hardening. Communist-era authorities divided the State Treasury-controlled land into geodesic plots, designating the western section for housing and building a bus station and streets elsewhere. In 1984, the Association of Maków Mazowiecki Lovers excavated matzevot previously used to pave streets; a 1987 stepped-pyramid monument by Wojciech Henrykowski, built from 250 recovered tombstones and fragments, now stands at the edge of the bus station's maneuvering area, still operated by the 'Mobilis' company since 2010.
